# Features by Data Plane: Linux Kernel and VPP

Ze can forward packets through the Linux kernel (`kernel`) or through VPP (`vpp`).
The primary selector (`interface backend`) chooses the deployment's
forwarding data plane. Every backend, FIB writer, feature, and YANG `ze:backend`
gate declares its plane requirement in code; `ze config validate`, commits,
reloads, daemon startup, and `ze doctor` (`doctor-dataplane-mismatch`) all judge
the configuration against the declarations listed below.

For how Ze starts and supervises VPP, see the [VPP guide](vpp.md).

## Data-Plane Selectors

Each component with pluggable forwarding backends declares a selector leaf and
the configuration roots it governs. When a secondary selector is active (set
explicitly, governing a present config root, or followed by an active table
producer), its value must match the primary data plane (`interface backend`).
An unused secondary selector at its default refuses nothing. Setting any
selector leaf to a value that no backend in this build registers is refused
with the schema default as the fix.

| Selector | Role | Governed roots | Schema default | Registered backends |
|----------|------|----------------|----------------|---------------------|
| `interface backend` | Primary data plane | `interface` | `kernel` | `kernel`, `vpp` |
| `firewall backend` | Secondary | `firewall`, `system conntrack` | `kernel` | `kernel`, `vpp` |
| `traffic control backend` | Secondary | `traffic control` | `kernel` | `kernel`, `vpp` |

## FIB Writers

Each FIB plugin declares `ProgramsFIB` and, when it targets a data plane, its
`DataPlane`. Without an explicit `fib` block, Ze loads the writer matching
`interface backend`. An explicit `fib` block always wins. A host-side
writer (`HostSideDataPlane: true`) programs the Linux host route table beside
the selected data plane: it is accepted beside a selected-plane writer (for
example `fib kernel` beside `fib vpp` under `interface backend vpp`), and
refused alone under another data plane with the selected-plane `fib` block as
the fix.

| Plugin | Config block | Data plane | Host-side | Behavior |
|--------|--------------|------------|-----------|----------|
| `fib-dummy` | `fib dummy` | none | no | No-plane choice; reaches no data plane by design, accepted under any primary selector, and refused beside any other FIB plugin. |
| `fib-kernel` | `fib kernel` | `kernel` | yes | Host-side Linux writer; accepted beside a selected-plane FIB block and refused alone on another plane. |
| `fib-p4` | `fib p4` | none | no | Explicit block only; declares no data plane and is not compared against the primary selector. |
| `fib-vpp` | `fib vpp` | `vpp` | no | Programs its declared data plane; refused when the primary selector chooses another plane. |

## Selector-Following Features

These features program rules through another component's backend selector (for
example firewall table producers). When any of them is active in the candidate
configuration or command-line `--plugin` selection, its governing selector must
match `interface backend`.

| Owner | Config path | Follows selector | Active when | Why |
|-------|-------------|------------------|-------------|-----|
| `anomaly-shape` | `anomaly shape` | `firewall backend` | config root present | anomaly shaping registers firewall tables |
| `copp` | `control-plane-protection` | `firewall backend` | config root present | control-plane protection registers firewall tables |
| `ddos-local` | `ddos local` | `firewall backend` | config root present | local DDoS mitigation registers firewall tables |
| `flowspec-firewall` | `flowspec-firewall` | `firewall backend` | plugin selected in config or `--plugin` | flowspec-firewall registers firewall tables |

## Fixed-Plane and Host-Side Features

Features without the host-side mark are refused at commit, `ze config validate`,
reload, and daemon start (and reported by `ze doctor` under
`doctor-dataplane-mismatch`) whenever `interface backend` selects
a plane outside their supported planes.

A feature marked host-side (`HostSideDataPlane: true`, such as `sysctl`) stays
accepted on any data plane: keys controlling Linux kernel behavior apply to the
host kernel on any data plane, while packet-forwarding keys such as `rp_filter`
act only on packets punted to Linux, not on packets forwarded by VPP.

| Owner | Config path | Supported planes | Host-side | Active when | Why |
|-------|-------------|------------------|-----------|-------------|-----|
| `flow-export` | `flow-export conntrack` | `kernel` | no | predicate matches config | the kernel conntrack table sees none of the flows VPP forwards |
| `flow-export` | `flow-export sampling` | `kernel` | no | predicate matches config | flow export sampling installs a kernel traffic-control filter |
| `gtsm` | `bgp` | `kernel` | no | predicate matches config | GTSM programs Linux kernel host routes and a kernel nftables drop table |
| `ike` | `vpn ipsec` | `kernel` | no | config root present | IPsec programs kernel XFRM only, and VPP forwards the packets, so the tunnels would carry no traffic |
| `l2tp` | `environment l2tp server` | `kernel` | no | predicate matches config | L2TP programs Linux PPP interfaces in the kernel only |
| `policy-routes` | `policy route` | `kernel` | no | config root present | policy routing programs Linux kernel ip rule entries and nftables marks |
| `sysctl` | `sysctl` | `kernel` | yes | config root present | sysctl sets the Linux kernel's own tunables |

## YANG `ze:backend` Feature Gates

The config engine walks the written configuration tree before schema defaults
are materialized and refuses any node whose `ze:backend` annotation excludes the
active backend of its governing selector. Narrowest annotation wins when a child
node overrides an enclosing container or list. Nodes without a `ze:backend`
annotation are not restricted by this walk.

## Backend Verifier Limits

Per-rule and per-qdisc compatibility limits are enforced in code by each VPP
backend verifier and stay hand-written beside their source anchors:

- [Firewall VPP compatibility and limits](firewall.md#vpp-backend-compatibility-and-limits): ACL and NAT44 filter/action limits, SNAT/masquerade source-match refusal, and commit-time verification of producer tables (`firewall-producer-tables`).
- [Traffic control VPP compatibility matrix](traffic-control.md#vpp-backend-compatibility-matrix): supported qdisc types, multi-class steering filters, root rate, mark filter, and ingress policer refusals.
- [VPP deployment guide](vpp.md): VPP daemon lifecycle, LCP pairing, WireGuard plugin requirement (`doctor-vpp-wireguard`), and dual-FIB host-side routing.
